body: Oil Traders Want U.S. to Release Sanctioned Tankers as Freight Costs Soar What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have prompted an increase in EV sales to avoid retail fuel inflation and gas demand destruction in favor of other power generation sources. With COP31 starting next week, some participants have signaled that faster electrification could become the focus of the event. “I would like to see a strong outcome on electrification in our presidency-led decision,” this year’s COP’s head of negotiations, Australian climate change minister Chris Bowen, told Bloomberg. Bowen also said he would consider COP31 a success if all participating countries made a commitment to increase the share of electricity in their final energy demand mix. Final energy is the kind that is actually used, as opposed to primary energy, which is energy in its raw form. While crude oil, for instance, is primary energy, gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel are final energy. Electricity is also a form of final energy, with its primary input coming from primary coal, gas, water, geothermal, and, more recently, solar and wind energy. It is those two latter sources of energy that COP leaders have selected as favorites for the grid of the near and far future—but have so far failed to make dominant. The world still sources over 80% of its primary energy from hydrocarbons. In other words, over 80% of the energy resources that the world consumes come from oil, gas, and coal. But, according to Bloomberg’s Zero podcast host, Akshat Rathi, by the time the energy goes from primary to final, the share of hydrocarbons falls to 65%. “Thus electrification is foremost an energy efficiency solution, because it reduces primary energy demand without cutting the useful outcomes that citizens want,” Rathi wrote in a recent report on COP31 ambitions. Electrification is the ultimate goal of the energy transition in every industry and aspect of life, excluding, perhaps chemicals production and related fields that rely on hydrocarbon feedstock for their output. Yet it is not just any electrification, of course, that transition advocates promote. Electrification must come from wind, solar, biomass, geothermal, hydro, and nuclear if it is to be done the right way, in view of emission reduction targets agreed a decade ago in Paris. Related: The Iran War Isn't Over, but Oil Traders Are Already Pricing In Peace Over these past ten years, trillions have been invested in the goal of electrification. Indeed, transition investment just last year hit $2.3 trillion, according to BloombergNEF . This was 8% higher than total transition investment during the previous year—and there was not even a war in the Middle East to cause the most serious disruption to oil and gas supply in history. The biggest portion of that total went into transport electrification, and the second-biggest portion went into wind and solar capacity. The buildout in electric vehicles, wind, and solar generation capacity and related technologies over the past 10 years has been quite impressive. It has failed to reduce global emissions of carbon dioxide, but it has led to regional declines, for instance in Europe, by means of energy demand destruction, mostly by discouragement through higher costs resulting from emission reduction policies. These higher costs appear to plague energy transition efforts—and the ultimate goal of near-total electrification of the world. “Electrification is an unquestionably good thing,” Australia’s Chris Bowen told Bloomberg’s Rathi. “Even if your grid is powered by coal and you don’t have solar panels at home, if you’re just charging [an electric car] off a coal-fired grid, you are reducing emissions by something like 60%.” Indeed, electric vehicles are widely seen as instrumental for the success of the electrification drive, but critics point o

Bessent says 'not necessarily' a mistake if the Fed hikes again
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined CNBC for an interview on Oct. 28, 2026.
body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that further Federal Reserve rate hikes wouldn't necessarily be a mistake. After CNBC's Brian Sullivan asked if rate increases in the future would constitute a monetary policy error, Bessent responded: "That's not necessarily so." Bessent's comments came hours after the Fed announced it would keep interest rates unchanged at its October gathering, as the market widely expected. Bessent is a key confidant of President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly called for lower interest rates. Trump pressured Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's predeccesor, Jerome Powell, over the issue during Powell's final months at the helm of the central bank. But Bessent said Wednesday that both he and Trump believe Warsh is doing well and can strike a balance between ensuring full employment and stable prices. "I think Chair Warsh is off to a great start," Bessent said. "As I often say, I have great confidence in him." The Fed's decision to hold rates steady came a month after it lifted borrowing costs for the first time in three years. Fed funds futures traders widely expected the central bank to return to rate hiking when it meets again in December. Bessent said he would like to see the Fed have an "open mind" about the supply shock from energy prices having a "transitory nature." The U.S. war with Iran has led to a sharp drop in global crude production volumes, in turn leading annual inflation readings to move further from the Fed's target of 2%. Bessent also said the U.S. efforts to isolate the Iran economy, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast , have been "very successful." He said internal estimates show that Iran's economy could contract by as much as 25% in the span of a year. When asked about bond yields on artificial-intelligence related debt, the Wall Street veteran said "we monitor" it, but that it didn't need to cause concern. Bessent specifically referenced neoclouds , a type of company providing specific cloud infrastructure supporting AI that has recently struggled in the market. Tesla CEO Elon Musk warned on Sunday that more than 200 neocloud firms "are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation." "I don't think it's problematic at all," Bessent said. "The neoclouds are a small component of the overall ecosystem, and we're still seeing the financing getting done. We're still seeing the deals get done." Bessent told CNBC he expects the third-quarter GDP data expected Thursday to be "strong." But he clarified that "I haven't seen it yet."

title: The UK cuts energy bills, taxes banks and boosts defense in high-stakes budget
summary: The U.K. budget cuts household energy costs, raises taxes on banks and directs billions toward defense, Ukraine and artificial intelligence
body: The U.K.'s finance minister John Healey delivered his first fiscal budget on Wednesday, announcing funding for defense, AI initiatives and measures designed to ease cost-of-living pressures. The Autumn Budget included dozens of measures aimed largely at easing rising costs for Britain's population, but Healey was careful not to risk the ire of markets, which responded broadly positively to his plans. As a net energy importer, the U.K. is vulnerable to external energy shocks. Inflation has risen sharply this year, with surging fuel costs driving the annual inflation rate to 3.5% in September. Markets expect the Bank of England to hike interest rates next month, while government borrowing costs have risen sharply this year. The U.K. government, led by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, had promised to alleviate economic pressures ahead of the budget. On Wednesday, Healey said he would deliver "breathing space" for families, saying the country needs "radical change on energy," and citing the inflationary impact of the U.S.-Iran war — a conflict he said "we did not want." His measures included the removal of standing charges on household gas heating bills, the extension of a tax break on electricity for millions of households through July 2027, and £100 ($133) checks for those living in the four lowest local housing tax bands. This will cost £2.6 billion. Healey said tariffs would be removed on over 100 grocery products, a policy announced before the budget was officially unveiled. Small business relief from business rates — a tax on commercial premises — would be extended to include more companies in the hospitality, retail and leisure sectors. Other measures included £15 million to provide books for children, funding aimed at reducing homelessness and support for people to purchase their first home. The U.K.'s minimum wage will rise by 3.9%, while a planned cut to tax-free savings thresholds was canceled. But Healey also pledged to bring down the welfare bill, pointing to reforms to pensions and sickness benefits. But he said he would not "write off a million young people [or] see disabled people suffer the indignities of a system that has been found 'not fit for purpose.'" The U.K.'s welfare bill, which reached 10.7% of UK GDP in 2024/25, has been a contentious issue in recent years. Previous finance minister Rachel Reeves watered down her own plans to cut welfare spending after a rebellion from lawmakers within her party. Healey also announced investments in developing — and regulating — the U.K.'s artificial intelligence industry. "Nowhere is the necessary role for the state clearer than in artificial intelligence," he said, as he announced hundreds of millions of pounds in funding for AI security and sovereignty. He announced a "covenant" for data centers in the country, with "strict tests" they must meet: "To invest in local communities, create local jobs and protect local water supplies. In return, critical data centers will get the grid connections they need, and, where necessary, be allowed to build onsite generation while they wait," Healey said. Healey also announced tax breaks for founders, including a reduced capital gains tax rate on gains of up to £10 million. Cash would also be injected into various regional hubs, Healey said, to "unleash Britain's innovation power." The budget also included £10 billion of additional economic and military support for Ukraine . "Today we send a clear message to Moscow: Britain will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes," he said. More funding would go to defense, he added, to ensure the country can meet its NATO spending commitments. "At the Spending Review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our NATO commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030," he said. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. It also approves a $1 billion stock buyback for MSTR Class A common shares, a $1 billion buyback program for Digital Credit Securities (consisting primarily of STRC preferred stock), an increase in the STRC dividend to 12% from 11.5%, and the USD Reserve Policy, which reserves $2.55 billion in cash along with the potential $1.25 billion from monetizing BTC for a $3.8 billion liquidity buffer. Strategy currently holds 847,363 bitcoin which cost a total of $64.10 billion, averaging $75,651 per BTC. The new Digital Credit Capital Framework permits the sale of up to 20,800 BTC, or approximately 2.5% of Strategy's total Bitcoin holdings, but it does not signify the company is selling BTC. Instead, it will provide flexibility for Management to monetize approximately 2.5% of Strategy's Bitcoin holdings to enhance the balance sheet or provide additional sources of liquidity in support of its future capital requirements. While this move marks a change in Strategy's capital management, it does not mean Strategy is abandoning its long-term strategy and focus on accumulating and holding Bitcoin. Over the past several years, Strategy funded most of its Bitcoin purchases through stock issuance when the company's stock traded at a significant premium to its Bitcoin. Now, as the premium has shrunk, issuing new shares at a discount will result in more dilution. This framework provides an additional alternative. The Class A buyback is simple: at $101 per share, Strategy is repurchasing stock at a level that signals a compressed mNAV, suggesting that the company's management believes its shares are a bargain relative to their bitcoin content, even at a 1x NAV premium. Meanwhile, the Digital Credit Securities repurchase, specifically buying back STRC at a discount to its $100 par value, aims to correct the preferred equity tier. Additionally, increasing the STRC dividend rate from 11.5% to 12% for all record dates on or after July 1 directly improves the yield and encourages buyers to step up to the $100 par level. The USD Reserve Policy answers the key concern of the preferred shareholders raised by the Rosen investigation: is Strategy capable of meeting its payments if bitcoin stays flat? title: NVIDIA Q1 FY2027: Revenue $81.6B Beat, Data Center +92%, but August 26 Guidance Test Will Prove Sustainability - TradingKey
body: Nvidia reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, up 85% year-over-year, driven by robust data center demand. Q2 guidance projects $91 billion in revenue, excluding China compute. While upcoming August 26 earnings and Vera Rubin production ramp-ups are critical catalysts, aggressive capital deployments—including a $1.5 billion investment and $105 billion lease guarantee with SB Energy, alongside participation in a $500 billion AI financing platform—significantly elevate the company's credit risk and balance-sheet exposure amid rising bond yields and shifting macroeconomic conditions. TradingKey - On May 20, Nvidia ( NVDA ) announced Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion that exceeded consensus and increased by 85 percent from last year while data center revenue reached $75.2 billion, an increase of 92 percent from the previous year. However, the stock price fell after earnings as investors had more serious questions. Is this level of growth sustainable? The answer to that question will become available during the August 26 earnings as we will know if the guidance will be met as the Vera Rubin production begins to ramp up, the SB Energy financing closed at $105 billion with strong and secure demand, and hyperscaler data center capex remains strong despite the increase in bond yields. Several developments in August have moved the needle. H200 chips began to reach China in small quantities, Nvidia invested $1.5 billion in SB Energy for securing 8 GW of Ohio infrastructure, and joined a $500 billion financing platform with BlackRock and Apollo. The new focus for Nvidia suggests that while this may drive near-term revenue, it may also increase credit risk. The upcoming Jackson Hole Fed meeting, scheduled for August 27-29, will be a good indicator of the overall economy. Q1 FY2027 revenue was $81.6 billion, an increase of 85 percent from last year, and 20 percent from the last quarter. Data Center revenue for the same period was $75.2 billion and increased by 92 percent from last year and 21 percent from the last quarter. Of this, revenue from hyperscale data center customers was $37.9 billion and from AI clouds, industrial, and enterprise customers was $37.4 billion. For the data center, the computing revenue was $60.4 billion and networking equipment revenue was $14.8 billion, an increase of 199 percent from the last year. GAAP gross margin was 74.9 percent. The 92 percent year over year growth can be attributed to the extraordinary demand for AI combined with constrained supply. Going forward, the guidance will exclude China data center compute (export controls still in effect). NVIDIA set $91.0B revenue for the second quarter of FY2027, reflecting ~12% midpoint sequential growth. The expected GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are 74.9% and 75.0%, respectively. Guidance also noted that there would be no data center compute revenue from China. Without this revenue contribution from China, any revenue contribution from China would signal a positive surprise, while sales from China would not count as a revenue miss. The upcoming August 26 earnings call will illustrate whether revenue goals for the second quarter were met, whether there are revenue goals for the third quarter, and whether goals were met for gross margin goals with the increasing price of inputs and the high capital spend. NVIDIA announced on August 17 that it would invest $1.5B and give up to $105B leasing guarantees in SB Energy (SoftBank subsidiary) for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike data center at an 8 GW Ohio campus. title: Intel Q2 2026: Revenue Up 25%, Data Center +59%, Stock Surges Then Retreats to $100 - TradingKey
body: Intel’s Q2 2026 results reflect a significant turnaround, highlighted by a 25% revenue increase and 59% growth in Data Center and AI segments. While a $12.5 billion non-cash CHIPS Act charge caused an $11 billion GAAP loss, non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 exceeded expectations. Despite operational progress, investor sentiment retreated due to concerns over negative free cash flow (-$8.4 billion) and aggressive capital expenditure guidance. While the company demonstrates strong core momentum, long-term stock performance depends on proving the foundry division’s path to profitability and successfully managing the high cost of capacity expansion. TradingKey - Intel ( INTC ) 's second-quarter 2026 results, reported on July 23, signal a major positive turning point in their two-year recovery effort. 16.1 billion dollars in revenue exceeded estimated consensus by 12% and had a year on year growth of 25%, being the highest growth in 15 years. Revenue from the Data Center and AI division grew 59%, reaching 6.3 billion dollars, and now makes up 39% of Intel's total revenue. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was 0.42, almost double the 0.21 estimated consensus. A large 12.5 billion dollar non-cash charge from the CHIPS Act caused a GAAP net loss of 11.0 billion dollars, substantially covering up for a lack of well-executed operations. The stock price soared a maximum of 13% to 112.70 dollars on July 23, only to retreat to around 100 dollars by early August, as investors tried to come to terms with the increased guidance for capex, the negative free cash flow, and the remaining significant losses from the foundry. The operational progress achieved was most important, but so was the high cost of capital. The operational story from Intel's Q2 2026 earnings call and the results that are very fresh and were published on July 23, say the following. Total revenues of $16.1 billion, which is 25% more than the previous year, and over $14.42 billion from the expected Wall Street consensus, mark the highest growth in the company in over 15 years. Based on the non-GAAP measure, Intel's net income for the quarter was $2.2 billion. Diluted EPS of $0.42 was almost double the estimate consensus of $0.21. It was a positive quarter with $7.0 billion in operational cash flow. However, and particularly in this case, the GAAP story must be told. Here the story is much worse, with an $11.0 billion net loss, or $(2.16) per diluted share of common stock. Losses were driven by a non-cash mark-to-market accounting loss on escrowed shares under the CHIPS Act Secure Enclave agreement of $12.5 billion. This is an accounting charge driven by the government funding agreement and is not a closing loss for the operating business. This one-time charge must be removed to assess the quality of the earnings for the operational quarter. This is also the reason non-GAAP earnings are relevant. The segment booked $6.3 billion in revenue, a 59% year-on-year and 24% quarter-on-quarter growth. This is the fastest ramp in Xeon 6 processors, attributed to the buildout of enterprise AI infrastructure and demand for agentic AI. The segment reported $6.3 billion in revenue with $2.5 billion in operating profit, resulting in a 40% operating margin. This is where Intel is winning, proving that the demand for AI infrastructure does not only include accelerators, but also server CPUs, networking, and packaging. Client Computing and Physical AI were up 13%, totaling $8.9 billion. Sales of premium AI PCs should continue to encourage Embedded’s steady growth. However, the foundry story is most convoluted. Intel Foundry’s revenue was $5.8 billion growing 31% year-on-year, but reported $2.1 billion in operating loss. title: SpaceX Stock Could Nearly Double — Analyst Says Nvidia Rubin Chips Could Fuel One-Year Payback - Stocktwits
body: Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) could nearly double as its Nvidia-powered AI expansion opens up a larger revenue opportunity, Oppenheimer says. SPCX stock fell 1% on Wednesday to $140.71, logging its second consecutive session in the red. Oppenheimer raised its SpaceX price target to $280 from $250, implying a 99% upside from current levels, and maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating. The firm identified SpaceX’s vertically integrated AI platform as a key differentiator. According to a report on Investing.com, the research firm said that the company owns valuable data, has access to substantial capital and Nvidia GPUs, and can build infrastructure rapidly. Oppenheimer said new Nvidia Rubin chips could pay for themselves in one year amid strong AI compute demand and pricing. SpaceX could retain 100% of the revenue generated through Cursor and Grok or capture around 50% when acting as an AI infrastructure wholesaler, the firm said. The Cursor acquisition has also strengthened SpaceX’s agentic coding data and reasoning capabilities, benefiting Grok Bot and Grok 4.6, with further improvements expected in Grok 5.0. Oppenheimer said AI usage and productivity are running ahead of expectations, although infrastructure remains the biggest bottleneck. The firm raised its long-term revenue estimates by about 10% on stronger compute pricing, compounding to 20% over time when combined with higher capex. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia recently detailed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system, targeting initial launches in the fourth quarter of 2027 and significant scaling in 2028. SpaceX’s first-gen Starmind AI1 satellite is designed around an orbital configuration of 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs. SpaceX also adopted standalone Vera CPUs for Grok’s agentic workloads on Earth, making Nvidia’s architecture the backbone of both its terrestrial Colossus-scale builds and orbital computing network. Deepwater’s Gene Munster estimated that SpaceX already contributes nearly $5 billion, or 5%, of Nvidia’s quarterly revenue, up from 3%. He said Nvidia may increasingly view SpaceX as a hyperscaler peer given its massive compute plans. Nvidia has also disclosed an ownership stake in SpaceX. SpaceX revealed the scale of its AI ambitions during its first public earnings call last month. The company expects to exceed 2 GW of computing capacity by the end of 2026 and move closer to 10 GW than 5 GW by the end of 2027. Its broader power-and-cooling pipeline totals 20 GW. Musk said SpaceX has committed to using Nvidia GPUs exclusively “because they are the best.” He also expects the company to receive a significant percentage of Nvidia’s GPU production next year. Melius Research estimated that even 2 GW of SpaceX’s planned buildout could generate $100 billion in incremental revenue for Nvidia. Meanwhile, the capital required for SpaceX’s 2027 expansion has been estimated at between $300 billion and $500 billion. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SpaceX has been ‘bearish’ over the past week amid a 16% decline in 24-hour message volumes. One bullish user said , “$SPCX Oppenheimer target is ridiculous” Another user noted , “$SPCX increased price targets and new contracts everyday, and this thing can barely clear the ipo price” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com.
